subject: maths
printing: Part I: Reprint 2026-27; Part II: First Edition October 2025
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF

topics.title: Lakhs and crores
outcomes: Learner can read and write large numbers in the Indian system (lakh, crore) and compare with the international system
misconceptions: Thinks 1 crore = 1 million
Places commas the international way while reading in lakhs
hooks: Population of your state; budget headlines in crores

topics.title: Exact and approximate values
outcomes: Learner can decide when an approximate value is appropriate and round to a sensible place
misconceptions: Believes rounded figures in news are "wrong"
hooks: "about 1.4 billion people" vs the exact census count

topics.title: Patterns in products
outcomes: Learner can estimate products of large numbers and spot patterns with powers of 10
misconceptions: Miscounts zeros when multiplying 3000 × 400
hooks: How many seconds in a year?

topics.title: Writing arithmetic expressions
outcomes: Learner can write expressions for situations and compare the values of expressions without full calculation
misconceptions: Thinks an expression must always be calculated before it can be compared
hooks: Bill for 3 samosas and 2 chai

topics.title: Terms, brackets and order of evaluation
outcomes: Learner can identify terms in an expression and evaluate expressions with brackets correctly
misconceptions: Evaluates strictly left to right (3 + 4 × 2 = 14)
Distributes a minus sign only to the first term inside brackets
hooks: Splitting a group restaurant bill

topics.title: Tenths and hundredths
outcomes: Learner can represent tenths and hundredths as fractions and decimals using measurement contexts
misconceptions: Reads 0.5 as "zero point five units" without linking it to 5/10
Thinks 0.5 and 0.05 are equal
hooks: Height in metres and centimetres; ₹ and paise

topics.title: Decimal place value
outcomes: Learner can explain the value of each digit in a decimal number
misconceptions: Believes the place names after the point are "oneths, tenths" mirroring the left side
hooks: Cricket overs 4.3 vs decimals: why 4.3 overs is not 4.3 in decimals

topics.title: Locating and comparing decimals
outcomes: Learner can place decimals on a number line and compare them
misconceptions: Thinks the longer decimal is larger (0.125 > 0.5)
Thinks the shorter decimal is larger because tenths are bigger than thousandths (0.4 > 0.45)
hooks: Which athlete was faster: 10.09 s or 10.9 s?

topics.title: Adding and subtracting decimals
outcomes: Learner can add and subtract decimals by aligning place values
misconceptions: Aligns digits from the right like whole numbers (2.5 + 1.25 = 1.50)
hooks: Adding prices on a grocery bill

topics.title: Letters standing for numbers
outcomes: Learner can use a letter to stand for an unknown or varying number and write expressions in words and symbols
misconceptions: Thinks a letter stands for an object (a = apples) rather than a number
Believes different letters must have different values
hooks: Cost of n pencils at ₹5 each

topics.title: Evaluating and simplifying expressions
outcomes: Learner can substitute values into expressions and combine like terms
misconceptions: Writes 2x for x = 3 as 23
Adds unlike terms (3a + 2b = 5ab)
hooks: Matchstick patterns: sticks needed for n squares

topics.title: Patterns and relationships with algebra
outcomes: Learner can describe a pattern with an algebraic rule and use it to predict
misconceptions: Believes a rule found from a few cases cannot be written generally
hooks: Calendar 2×2 box: why do diagonal sums match?

topics.title: Intersecting lines and vertically opposite angles
outcomes: Learner can identify linear pairs and vertically opposite angles and use their properties
misconceptions: Thinks vertically opposite angles are the angles one above the other
hooks: Angles made by a pair of open scissors

topics.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
outcomes: Learner can identify parallel and perpendicular lines and draw them
misconceptions: Thinks lines are parallel only if they are the same length
Believes two lines that do not meet within the page are parallel
hooks: Railway tracks; ruled lines in a notebook

topics.title: Transversals: corresponding and alternate angles
outcomes: Learner can identify corresponding and alternate angles and use them to test for parallel lines
misconceptions: Assumes corresponding angles are equal even when lines are not parallel
hooks: A road crossing two parallel canals

topics.title: Parity
outcomes: Learner can use odd/even reasoning to decide whether something is possible
misconceptions: Thinks the sum of three odd numbers can be even
hooks: Can 5 friends shake hands so each shakes an odd number of hands?

topics.title: Explorations in grids and magic squares
outcomes: Learner can construct and reason about magic squares and grid puzzles
misconceptions: Believes magic squares are found by trial and error only
hooks: The magic square at Parshvanath temple, Khajuraho

topics.title: Virahanka–Fibonacci numbers
outcomes: Learner can generate the Virahanka sequence and explain it through counting rhythms
misconceptions: Thinks the sequence was first discovered in Europe
hooks: Counting rhythms of short and long beats in Sanskrit poetry

topics.title: Digits in disguise
outcomes: Learner can solve simple cryptarithms by reasoning about place value and carries
misconceptions: Assumes each letter can be any digit, ignoring carries
hooks: Decode SEND + MORE style puzzles

chapters.title: A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines

topics.title: Constructing triangles
outcomes: Learner can construct triangles given three sides and check when a triangle is possible (triangle inequality)
misconceptions: Believes any three lengths can make a triangle
hooks: Can you make a triangle with sticks of 3, 4 and 9 cm?

topics.title: Altitudes of triangles
outcomes: Learner can draw the altitude of a triangle from a vertex, including when it falls outside
misconceptions: Thinks an altitude must lie inside the triangle
hooks: The height of a tent

topics.title: Types of triangles and the angle sum
outcomes: Learner can classify triangles by sides and angles and use the angle-sum property
misconceptions: Believes bigger triangles have larger angle sums
hooks: Tear corners of a paper triangle and line them up

topics.title: Multiplying fractions
outcomes: Learner can multiply fractions and interpret "of" using area models
misconceptions: Believes multiplication always makes the answer bigger
hooks: 1/2 of 3/4 of a cake

topics.title: Dividing fractions
outcomes: Learner can divide by a fraction and explain why it is multiplying by the reciprocal
misconceptions: Thinks division always makes the answer smaller
Inverts the first fraction instead of the divisor
hooks: How many 1/4 kg packets from 3 kg of dal?

topics.title: Problems with fractions
outcomes: Learner can solve multi-step real-life problems involving fractions
misconceptions: Applies the last operation learnt instead of reading the situation
hooks: Sharing land in a will; recipes for more people

topics.title: Congruent figures
outcomes: Learner can decide whether two figures are congruent by superposition
misconceptions: Thinks figures are congruent if they look similar in shape, regardless of size
hooks: Two identical rotis vs a big and small roti

topics.title: Congruence criteria for triangles
outcomes: Learner can use SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS to show triangles are congruent and know why SSA fails
misconceptions: Believes AAA guarantees congruence
hooks: Why bridge trusses use triangles

topics.title: Angles of isosceles and equilateral triangles
outcomes: Learner can use congruence to show that base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal
misconceptions: Thinks only equilateral triangles have equal angles
hooks: A-frame roofs of hill houses

topics.title: Multiplying integers
outcomes: Learner can multiply integers and explain the sign rules using patterns and contexts
misconceptions: Thinks negative × negative should be negative
hooks: Patterns in a multiplication table extended below zero

topics.title: Dividing integers
outcomes: Learner can divide integers and connect division to multiplication
misconceptions: Believes division by a negative number is impossible
hooks: A temperature drop of 12 °C over 4 hours

topics.title: Highest common factor
outcomes: Learner can find the HCF of numbers by listing and by prime factorisation, and solve problems
misconceptions: Finds the lowest common factor (always 1) instead of the highest
hooks: Largest tile that fits a room exactly

topics.title: Lowest common multiple
outcomes: Learner can find the LCM and use it for problems of repetition
misconceptions: Confuses HCF and LCM in word problems
hooks: When will two buses leaving every 12 and 18 minutes meet again?

topics.title: Properties and procedures
outcomes: Learner can explain the relationship HCF × LCM = product of two numbers
misconceptions: Thinks the relation holds for three numbers as well
hooks: Check with 12 and 18

topics.title: Multiplying decimals
outcomes: Learner can multiply decimals and place the decimal point using estimation and fractions
misconceptions: Believes multiplying by 0.5 makes a number bigger
hooks: Cost of 2.5 kg potatoes at ₹32.40/kg

topics.title: Dividing decimals
outcomes: Learner can divide decimals by whole numbers and decimals
misconceptions: Thinks dividing by 0.5 halves the number
hooks: How many 0.25 l glasses from 3 l of juice?

topics.title: Questions and statements from data
outcomes: Learner can frame questions that data can answer and check statements against data
misconceptions: Believes data always proves a claim
hooks: Is it true that it rains more in July in your city?

topics.title: Representative values: mean, median, mode
outcomes: Learner can compute mean, median and mode and choose a suitable representative value
misconceptions: Thinks the mean must be one of the data values
Ignores extreme values that distort the mean
hooks: Average runs per match of a cricketer

topics.title: Visualising data
outcomes: Learner can draw and interpret double bar graphs and judge misleading graphs
misconceptions: Trusts a graph without checking its scale
hooks: Compare boys’ and girls’ favourite games

topics.title: Geometric constructions
outcomes: Learner can construct perpendicular bisectors, angle bisectors and specific angles with ruler and compass
misconceptions: Thinks a construction is the same as measuring with a protractor
hooks: Bisect an angle to cut a slice of pizza fairly

topics.title: Tilings
outcomes: Learner can identify shapes that tile the plane and explain using angles at a point
misconceptions: Believes any regular polygon can tile a floor
hooks: Hexagonal floor tiles; honeycomb

topics.title: Forming equations
outcomes: Learner can write simple linear equations for word problems
misconceptions: Writes the equation in the order the words appear, even when the meaning is reversed
hooks: Think-of-a-number tricks

topics.title: Solving equations systematically
outcomes: Learner can solve linear equations by doing the same operation on both sides and check the solution
misconceptions: Moves terms across "=" without changing the operation
Thinks the unknown is always on the left
hooks: Balance scale with weights

topics.title: Mind the mistake
outcomes: Learner can spot and correct errors in someone else’s solution
misconceptions: Believes a solution is correct if the final line looks neat
hooks: Play "find the bug" in a friend’s working
